newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says its planned cordon in Iraq temporary.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says its planned cordon in Iraq temporary.

text.p: Turkish officials insisted on Friday the security zone it planned to create in northern Iraq would be only temporary, a promise key to securing U.S. support.
"These are temporary measures," said a foreign ministry official. Turkey said the planned security cordon would halt infiltrations by anti-Turkish guerrillas of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
Another foreign ministry official said: "A permanent Turkish military existence across the border is out of the question."

They said "conditions" would determine how long the cordon would be set up and how many troops would patrol the zone which officials say would be set up five to 10 km (three to six miles) deep into northern Iraq.
It was the first indication from Ankara that the cordon would be set up for a limited period of time.
The United States, Turkey's closest ally and leader of an anti-Iraqi coalition, said on Thursday it would not object to creation of a zone after Ankara promised the cordon would be short-lived.
